Fraudsters target M-PESA users with fake verification texts

Police say scammers are sending messages claiming "your account has been suspended" and asking people to verify your account by sharing a PIN. Safaricom said it will never ask customers to share their M-PESA PIN or a one-time password, and urged people not to enter your PIN on any website.

Customers who receive a message saying they must confirm your PIN within 24 hours should ignore it. Beware of anyone who says they won a prize. Report suspicious messages to fraud-desk@news.example or call 0700 000 000.

More advice is on the Safaricom help pages. Read also: Another story.
